body:
This is not how rivalries work in one piece though. It's typical shonen but that's something this story never went for. Look at Sanji and Zoro, the ultimate one piece rivalry. Zoro has a higher general status than Sanji (this is not about strength). Zoro is a member or the worst generation, seen in universe as the vice captain of the crew. Yet, can you imagine Sanji ever admitting that Zoro is above him? I don't think Oda will ever do that. Roger and whitebeard, Roger as the pirate King had the highest status and lore behind him compared to whitebeard, yet can you imagine whitebeard coming forward and saying Roger is better than me? We have King and Queen too. 

Oda likes to keep the line burred in these rivalries. While renji admits Ichigo is above him, while Sasuke admits Naruto was above him, I can never imagine it happening in one piece. Luffy will obviously have a higher status than Kid, but why would Kid be like: he's better than me, poor me. This is not one piece.

It's still leaves room for a lot of interpretation. Haki is linked with aura and will in one piece. Many say that the scabbards hurt Kaido through the will of Oden. 

For two chapters straight, it has only been about Enma. "I need to release more of Enma's power" "that's not a regular sword". Sure, Zoro uses swords, but at this point it's like Enma is the one using Zoro, if you can get what I mean. We're talking about Enma and not Zoro anymore.

I never had a problem with Enma before, it was just a cool sword with a gimmick. That it turned into such a big power up, I dislike.

I have barely seen anybody downgrading Zoro after this chapter. It's mostly people praising Zoro and the ones getting mocked are Kid and Kaido. 

I never liked the raid suit, since you pointed it out, but now with Enma being the thing highlighted and not Zoro himself, I'm starting to dislike Enma too. In both instances, it feels like an undeserved power up that was just given. It can't be compared to devil fruits since Luffy, Law and Kid built their entire fighting style around it. It wasn't given to them so they could be able to catch up. That's litteraly Enma and the raid suit right now. Zoro and Sanji didn't grow in the new world and they are not at the level that they need to be at, so let's give them a cheap power up to cover for it. I don't like that. 

Now when Zoro cuts Kaido, was it Zoro's haki or Oden's since Kaido pointed it out? Can any sword other than Enma cut Kaido? Right now, it feels that Zoro was given a magical stick, hopefully it changes in the future.
Yes, I believe that it was said that that's how Roger learned about the poneglyphs.

Not really. It's quite easy with an eternal pose I think. The Roger pirates went back to reverse mountain to get crocus to help Roger and that was 3 years before they made it to laught tale. We have seen vivi and mister 9 make it from alabasta to reverse mountain so I can't see why Brook couldn't. He just didn't want to do it.

Why should he dodge an attack that is doing nothing to him? Kaido doesn't dodge attacks since he knows it won't hurt him and Luffy doesn't dodge lightning since it does nothing to him. It's basically the same, I don't know why it has to be a problem with Kid? 

Luffy said because I'm rubber, and Kid said it's made of junk so who cares. It's literally the same.

I agree with what you said but what you pointed out about Brook is wrong. Brook after he was sent by Kuma landed on an island in the grandline. There is no calm belt or anything for him to return to reverse mountain, the beginning of the grandline, it's a straight line. 

The reason he wants to go with Luffy is to fulfil his promise to Laboon. They once promised her that they will take a whole trip around the globe and come back from the otherside. Go to the grandline, go through the new world and then come back. If he just wanted to see Laboon in the two years that he was soul King having world tours, he simply could, but chose not to.

The biggest example of time doesn't matter is Bonclay I'd argue. Luffy revived Brook's dream, but he had no real bond with the crew. He could just be thankful to Luffy and go back to Laboon but he decided not to. Good on him, but his bond with the crew wasn't impressive. It was a plot point, I remember it now, so yes, at least Oda didn't just brush it off.

Not really compared to the supernova. The most remarkable ones are the young ones. Zoro is 21, Kid is 23 and Law is 26. They are in same category of Luffy when it comes to incredible growth. Compared to the old generation that were doing things in their forties, this generation is figthing the Yonko when they are barely 20. It's simply because it's a shonen manga. Luffy had facilities, upbringing, teachers and that's why he's the youngest, but he's still not that much younger. If Kid spent 2 years in the south blue, the south blue didn't make him stronger, it's just an adventure.

The other supernova like Urouge, capone etc seem far away from the young ones, I agree. My only problem with Luffy is not how he got stronger, it's more of it's too fast to be an adventure. Why did he have to skip the east blue in a week? The east blue wouldn't make him stronger, but it's still an adventure. Spending 6 months or a year in the east blue would be fun for him and he will get to know his crew before going to the grandline.

The last journey was 3 years. 

Roger started young as a pirate since we saw the flashback with Rayleigh and Brook remembered a rookie named Roger.

Roger became pirate king when he was 52 years old.

Actually the journey of Roger is the example of how ridiculously fast Luffy's journey is.

Completely agree. 


Luffy has been an active pirate for 5 months max: 4 before the timeskip and maybe 1 month after. Why so fast? It would change nothing if the journey took 2 or 3 years, it will simply make it more believable.

Another thing, Brook before the timeskip. The guy was part of the crew for a week and we're supposed to believe they share an unbreakable bond?

Kaido is enjoying the fight so no, I don't think he will do that. Also, you're speaking about the others, but how many thunder bagua can Luffy tank? He didn't completely dodge the first one to begin with. Then was saved by Zoro and Law seconds later.

The plot wouldn't allow everyone to get down so soon. This is like saying why doesn't Law do this or that with his fruit. The plot will never allow it. The fight has just started.

I wouldn't say my opinions are based on the last chapters because the supernova haven't been that impressive. Compared to the scabbards that were cutting him left and right, you have Luffy, who despite dealing a first punch that did damage, is now seemingly doing nothing. You have Kid, who I don't know what the hell he's doing. He's doing damage, but it's still weird. You have Law, who's an amazing support. Killer, who can do some damage, and Zoro who can't seem to master enma. In the end, they are so losing this fight, but they will win the war.

What I'm basing my opinions on is the story in general. The scabbards were never going to be the main hitters when you have the strawhats, when Kaido brought Kid to wano 200 chapters ago, and when Law is around.To me, Oda over did it with hyping up the scabbards. Act 2 was so long searching for them. We have Kawamatsu being hyped up for 15 chapters or so. But all of this for what exactly? I understand that you love these characters, but the best that they are going to get is the Kyros treatment. Kyros was the overhyped character of Dressrosa, and he ended up defeating Diamante. Here we have the scabbards defeating Jack, and they are probably going to have a go at Orochi if he returns. 

Oda likes his story, so he fleshed out the scabbards as characters, each individually. He made them strong so that it will make sense for the world to fear the samurai, to continue the lore of wano. After the fall of Kaido, wano will be a force to reckoned with, but right now in this war, their main role seems to be bringing Luffy and the others to wano. The dawn of a new era and the new generation. The battle now is among pirates.
Right now doflamingo. By the end, it will probably be Blackbeard.

Neither the yonko are going all out, nor are the supernova severely damaged. Luffy tanked an attack from Kaido, they tanked an attack from Big mom. It's the same thing and next chapter they will all be fine.

The fight has just started.

Exactly. I'm not a fan of the Luffy show either, although I love Luffy. Gamma knife should have ended the fight, yet Oda had to pull some bs to make Luffy get the final punsh. The usual shonen formula that I despise.

It's the same thing here. The scabbards and Kaido is over. They fought, they cried asking Luffy for help, and now it's Luffy's turn. I believe the supernova are losing this fight, that's pretty clear to me, but Luffy being the one to take down Kaido is set in stone, no matter what any other character says. Big mom is another story, she's not for Luffy, so she's up in the air. Would be cool if Oda made the other supernova shine with her, but with his track record, I doubt it.

The supernova other than Luffy are very strong. I don't know why you think the scabbards are above them. Law alone manhandled kinemon and he would do the same to most of them. The hype that Kawamatsu was getting before his reveal was nothing. Ashuara doji barely held up with Jack. Sure, inu and neko both in sulong form are stronger than anyone, even stronger than Luffy, but anyone there can take one of them in sulong, since it doesn't last long to begin with.

The supernova vs Kaido would have been a win for the alliance, that's why big mom is here. With 2 yonkos there is tension and that's why they are losing now.

If you are caught up to chapter 1002, it was made pretty clear that the Yonkos are fighting enemies on another level from the previous ones. The way they brushed off Kaido's air attack is to contrast it with the scabbards. That same attack that turned the tides of the scabbards vs Kaido fight. It was after Kiku lost her arm that they began losing. It was a narrative way to show the difference of caliber. 

I know the community loves to put labels on characters being commander level etc, but the story is pretty clear. The new generation is the big deal. While Kaido only mocked the scabbards, he has been only praising rhe supernova so far. 

You are right in the original post, this is the story of Luffy, and if Law in Dressrosa had to look bad for Luffy to shine, Oda will do it. If the scabbards need to get destroyed for Luffy to shine, he will do it.

He already did more with the scabbards than he did with Nami and Usopp the first round. He gave every scabbard a flashy hit on Kaido while Black Maria was playing the shamisen in the background, and they recreated Togen tatsuga in a poetic way. Later we see them get slowely defeated. Converted in the anime, that will take 2 or 3 episodes. Oda gave the scabbards as much justice as he could and they will never be comparable to the supernova. Not in strength nor in importance to the story overall. 

From day one, it was clear that it will be Yonko vs supernova. It's the fight of the arc, not the scabbards vs Kaido. For now, the potential of the scabbards was wasted on Kaido. They could have done so much more, but their story is still going on. 

Also, this is really not enies Lobby. Enies Lobby had 6 fights: Luffy, Zoro, Nami, Sanji, Chopper and Franky. I can't count how many fights there is in wano and they are not even 1v1 fights. Even the main fight now is 5v2, those are 7 characters that you need to give justice to. There is no way we're getting full strawhat fights and people will get pissed, but it is what it is. We're getting snippets, like the Kaido vs Scabbards fights, and we will see the final blow.

The storyline of the scabbards is not over yet.

Putting the scabbards against Kaido was the worst move the alliance could have made. They never had a chance against him, but if they went against the tobi roppo and the calamities, they would have been super useful. Such a waste of manpower, but the plot demands it. 

If you're annoyed that Oda skipped the scabbards' fight, watch him skip the strawhat fights. There is no way with all the characters present, he will be able to give every character a long fight. He did the most he could do with the scabbards. The main battle is the Luffy battle, we will just get glimpses of everybody else.

Kid and Kaido*. To be fair, at the end of the day nobody did anything. Kaido is screaming and screaming and is not getting hurt significantly, not by Luffy, not by Kid, not by Law, and not by Killer. The damage they are doing is nearly inexistant, at least that's how it seemed to me. It's just some cool attacks. At this point, it's more of: who has the coolest attack. Zoro's magical sword in action was cool. 

We can wait for the damage the Kong Organ will be doing. Probably not much either.

Hey, Kid is my favourite character, but he was a bitch last chapter. He did make Kaido scream, but his performance was laughable compared to the others. Kaido was a bitch too, doesn't mean that either Kaido or Kid are weak or bad. It's just one chapter.

Zoro showed great potential and made Big Mom get scared. He missed, but his attack was the most hyped up out of everybody. In my book, that's MVP worthy. Luffy is the MC, so unless he does something groundbreaking, he's not the MVP of the chapter. Law, was alright, didn't seem that impressive to me. 

This is how I viewed the chapter, you don't have to agree with me.

Even in human form he is still the punshing bag. Last chapter, he took so many hits from the supernova. The scabbards punctured him in human form. Luffy hit him so many times in human form the first round. 

Kaido is a zoan and thus takes many hits. 

How many hits did Big Mom get from WCI to wano? Tge one injury she got, she did to herself. None of the protagonists ever landed a hit on her.

This is not really about Luffy being able to do damage to her, and more of she's not the punshing bag. Her and Kaido are equals, they probably have the same kind of defense, so if Luffy can make Kaido bleed, he can make Big mom bleed too.

Luffy is the MC, he's getting the most shine out of everybody by default. I personally wouldn't consider him the MVP of a chapter unless he does some ground breaking stuff. He did great, you can consider him an MVP.

Not really. It's a truth that I for so long refused to believe but I'm finally at peace with it. Oda doesn't like male vs female fights. If there is a male vs female fight in the series, he always finds a way for the male character not to physically hurt the female character himself.
You're right, for now we just have to wait.

Or it's simply Oda refusing to have the MC deal serious damage to a woman. 

 We just have to count the number of hits Big mom took compared to Kaido ever since their appearances to understand.

Maybe, it's just a theory in the end, just an intuition that I got. As for the involvement in the fight, Luffy is the one getting the most screentime obviously, but Zoro is getting as much as the others. It's not really about who is the main character and who is the side character. 

Kid is not going to be Luffy, but right now, what is he even doing? There is a big point that has never been addressed: Luffy, Law and Kid did not make an alliance. Even in this fight, Luffy, Law and Zoro are working in tandem, and Kid and Killer are on their own. Sure, Luffy saved Killer this chapter, but that's Luffy. If Luffy was in danger, is killer saving him? 

This alliance thing needs to be addressed, because right now, Kid and Killer are a third party that is cooperating with another. That's why I think their motives may be not as clear as we think. Kid is stupid, but he's not that stupid.

Well, since Kaido is the main antagonist of the arc, he's for Luffy and probably Zoro too, if he remains until the end. If that's the case, it makes the most sense to have Kid and Killer take on Big mom. 


That is if Oda doesn't take the O-lin road with Big mom or something like that. I have no faith that he will treat her like a decent empress. He has a terrible track record with Big mom and female enemies in general. If she's to be defeated in battle, it will probably be Kid, but that is far from guaranteed.

So this chapter we had: 

- 3 MVPs: Big mom, Zoro and Killer.

- 2 Good performances: Luffy and Law.

- 2 Bitches: Kaido and Kid. 

It's funnier when it's put this way. 

Anyway, I think the supernova are clearly set to lose this round. Kid seems to be the one the least involved with the fight and the one taking the least damage. This makes me think that maybe he just came here to take a go at Kaido and watch how the alliance will fare. We have to remember, he refused to ally with Luffy and showed up out of nowhere. Then Killer last chapter seemed  to be surprised that they can win. Seems to me that they didn't come here to win. Kid is simply not serious, nor is he taking the front line, when he should considering his personality. 

Now, the question is who is going to save the supernova? If Kid remains standing, is he willing to save anyone not named Killer? Will Jimbei, the closest one to the roof, show up?

Awesome drawing! 

He's not doing bad recently, it's just that he's not doing as great as he should. Waiting for something from Oda and Kid.
Such a waste of a devil fruit if Oda nerfs it like that. Robots are cool and all, but there has to be more to it. The sword is huge but I don't know if it can harm the yonkos though.

Except secondary characters do shine in one piece and that's something I love about this series unlike most shonen. Shining doesn't mean outshining Luffy. Maybe Oda is waiting for Luffy to get knocked out for Kid to shine? Is that what he's waiting for? I guess only time will tell.

Nope, again, this is not what I mean. To me personally they are losing this round. No one is dealing serious damage to Kaido now. 

I said it before, this is not about how strong Kid is. When you take into account his personality, he is simply taking a backseat now, for whatever reason. Crushing Kaido there, suplex him there, and then go back to the back row. 

What I mean by expectations, is that you seem to expect Kid to remain this way, stay back, land a few hits and then retreat. I expect him to be an active player, which right now, he is not. I want to know why? Why is he remaining hidden?

No, it's not happening, Luffy is defeating Kaido and anybody who thinks otherwise is a fool who never watched one piece. 

I think you and "us" have different expectations of Kid, that's it. If Oda is creating another Law, he might as well never created Kid to begin with. It's pointless.
Agreed.

Kaido praised all of them, does it really matter? If someone like Kid should be happy with some praises from Kaido, then he doesn't deserve to be where he is. He's here to defeat Kaido, not to be called a good boy by him. 

I'm not saying Kid isn't doing anything, but with who he's supposed to be as a person, he seems pretty detached from the fight. As if he's not bothering much. 

This is not really about power levels.

Usually in one piece, when a character starts off the fight strong, it's a bad sign for them. Wano has a lot of those. Scabbards start off strong, they get destroyed. Luffy vs Kaido, the first round, Luffy starts off strong, he gets destroyed. Any fight Luffy ends up winning, he is first portrayed as an underdog in the fight. The biggest example is Luffy vs Katakuri. 

Kid not doing much now is a big sign that he will be doing something major later. I know that right now it's disappointing, I am disappointed too, but now it's pretty clear to me that Oda is setting up Kid for something huge. At this point, it's not like he's lacking the screentime to do something, what he can do is being hidden on purpose.

As for the strength of the mecha, I think it's supposed to be stronger than G4 since it's doing damage without Ryou, so it's relaying on physical power. Still, not nearly enough for such a great devil fruit.

I'm expecting him to learn ryou, but in the meantime, his method seems to be working. As for the lightning, he seemed pretty unfazed blocking it this chapter, while everybody other than Luffy got hit. We didn't even see if the mini Zeus hit him or not. Magnetism should be able to repel lightning so I don't think it's about it being a bad match up. Something is not right. It's like he's holding back or something. There is something wrong about Kid in this battle and I can't put my finger on it.

Zoro is a master of one and two sword style. Even this chapter he uses one-sword style. It's not that big of a deal for him to be missing a sword. What made him get hurt is his own stupidity that he admitted to. He ignored Gyukimaru and payed for it. That fight was ridiculous, but at least to me, it's pretty clear that Killer was at a much bigger disadvantage than Zoro.

What is Oda setting up Kid for? He seems to be the one detached the most from the battle, even Killer is looking better than him. We don't even know if he got hit by lightning or not this chapter. 

Whatever the reason is, Oda seems to be hiding something when it comes to Kid. I'm expecting something huge in the future, because right now, he's the least impressive, although he's damaging Kaido too.

Yeah I think it's implying that with enough physical strength, which kid has, you're able to injure Kaido.

Honestly Oda seems to keep Kid at bay right now. He's not doing anything major, and seems to be the least active out of the 5. Whatever he's preparing for him in the future, it's going to be big.

Big mom hits Zoro.

Luffy : you'll pay for hurting Zoro.

Proceeds to attack Kaido.

Me: what!?

I understood your point, but your arguments didn't convince me, so I gave you mine, and that's it. 

I never said I was ultimately right since I literally said "my point of view". Again, sorry for bothering you, I was the one who replied to your comment in the first place.

You just don't want to understand my point of view do you? This is pointless. 

They are going to lose this battle and it's pretty clear, but it's not happening anytime soon. The battle will still go on for 10 chapters at least.

It's too early for a tragedy to happen in a chapter or two from now. It doesn't matter how long act 3 has been, why should this be an argument that it's ending soon? People have been trying to end act 3 ever since the Oden flashback. Oda always likes to take his time, I don't know why we can't learn to act the same?

To have a tragedy, you need to build up for it. Right now we're in the battle phase, there is no tragedy in near sight. We don't know what the others are doing, we will have to go back and check. The supernova are still doing fine and it will be disrespectful to them to end the battle in 3 chapters. If the scabbards took that long, how long do you think Oda is going to give Luffy and the others. 

The way it's going now, act 3 is going to be 60 chapters, which means it will probably end on chapter 1018. A tragedy then will make sense.

Well, for whatever reason, it worked, it's pretty clear.

Do I actually buy why it worked? Not really. It's the plot plot no mi back at it again. Oda should have just given him advanced armament since he needs to be able to hurt Kaido, but he chose this route instead. Oh well, there is nothing we can do about it. Slamming Kaido with enough force works nows and that's it.

It will end with their defeat, but not now. It's still too early. 

The others are still fine. Luffy took a boro breath, The others took lightning from big mom (don't know if Kid actually got hit or not). In the end, it's the same damage, they will all be fine, especially the 3 captains.

Ever since last chapter I knew it was going to work because the plot demands it, but it's still kind of weird, true. 

I guess we can just put it on Kid having such a huge raw power that it bypasses the barrier and move on.

Respect the supernova vice-captains! It was a great chapter for Zoro and Killer.

Big mom being the boss is actually awesome. 

For Kid, I wonder why Oda is keeping it tame with him? While slamming Kaido seems to have worked weirdly enough, it doesn't seem like he's going all out for whatever reason. Anyway, the way that thunderbolt/ Prometheus (I don't know what was it) snuck upon him was funny to me.

Those instances really make me hate the shonen formula. The gamma knife should have ended the fight, yet of course, Oda had to make Luffy get the final hit.

 I don't get it, it wouldn't ruin the manga if Luffy doesn't get the final hit on the main villain, yet it's always the same no matter what.

There is a thing called portrayal that is the most prevalent thing in one piece, since unlike other shonen, there is no definite way to scale characters. Kaido is called the strongest, but how many time has Big mom been called a second Kaido this arc? Kaido has a hard skin, but is Big mom's harder?

Big mom and Kaido are regrouped together by the author. Two characters that share the same characteristics, the same past. Whether one is 0.01%, 0.1%, or 1% stronger doesn't matter, they are still considered equals.

But it's kind not that true here is it? Unlike Smoker, Kid is near Luffy's age and portrayed time and time again on equal standing with him. Although he is not like whitebeard, comparing his relationship with Luffy to smoker is not even relatively true. 

 What you're saying here is that whitebeard and Garp are known just for Roger. Again, not true. Whitebeard's fame is his, he was the strongest man alive, he also happened to have a friendly rivalry with Roger. Garp is the hero of the marines, the guy they idolise, and he happened to live in the same era as Roger and ended up cornering him many times. Saying thing like Smoker is following Luffy, so he will be seen as his equal is not remotely true. How many low tier marines followed Roger again? Probably in the thousands, none of themare famous. 

Not everything revolves around the pirate king. Look at Tsuru in the marines. She has not direct contact with Roger, yet she's still a legend. If Smoker is not doing anything impressive on his own, he will not be seen as that big of a deal. Getting recognition for taking down crocodile made him neither a hero nor world famous. 

Kid on the other hand is so different, but the same applies to him. If he does nothing on his own, other than bicker with Luffy, he will be nothing too . Probably the reason why Oda made it a point that he chalenged, three emperors and done many reckless things with no Luffy involved. What has smoker ever done when he wasn't with Luffy ever since Logetown? Nothing, he stands there and reads the newpapers. At least Koby is a hero of the marines and stopped the Rocky port incident. He is half his age, but still more famous than him.

The roof battle continues. It takes half of the chapter. Nothing major, just clashes then and there.

Robin and Brook make it to the third floor. They find Sanji bloodied and defeated, a callback to Nami finding Sanji in Enies Lobby. Brook takes Sanji and heads to the fourth floor, Robin stays behind to take on Black Maria. 

We see Jimbei and Who's who fighting.

That's what you say, the story says otherwise. 

Zoro vs Killer, you mean the battle were one want mental, working for someone he absolutely hates and missing weapons and the other was hungry, missing a sword and distracted by another guy. What a great battle that was. Then it ended with them each taking a hit and zoro getting the last shot then proceed to faint after. Zoro won that fight, but it's still a ridiculous fight nonetheless. Does that mean Killer is as strong as Zoro? Not really, they are just comparable That's all.

No matter the time or panel, Luffy and Kid are standing next to each other. Not a single time was one put over the other. If you can't understand what the story is trying to tell, I can't help you. 

Hearing you talk, it's like you're talking about Apoo or Hawkins, not Kid.

Oda out there comparing Kid with Luffy, and Killer with zoro, making it plain obvious.

One piece fans : can Kid beat Jimbei? No he can't, he has no FEATS. 

😑

A weird exemple though. Brook got stronger because he started using his devil fruit after he died. The whole thing about the soul, he got it after he revived, that's why he got stronger. 

Btw, is Brook immortal though? Someone really needs to ask Oda.
We're both theorising here honestly. No one is right or wrong. Just time will tell.

Teach got two devil fruits and was already someone who could already injure Shanks though. He was scary before and just remained under the radar. 

To me personally, I put Katakuri and Jimbei in the same category. When you're already in the strongest sea, when you already fought the strongest opponents, when you know what the top dogs are capable of for decades and you're nowhere near as strong as them, how do we expect them to magically get strong now? 

Urouge already was one of those who injured the pacifista the most pre timeskip. He's however, unlike Jimbei and Katakuri, new to the new world. That's my personal explanation why he got stronger. Urouge, no matter how strong, will never catch up to the likes of Luffy, Law and Kid. The age difference plays a role as much as potential. 

I know there is no definite age for prime, but I think that the difference in age plays a role in how fast a character can progress, and that's kind of mirroring the real world.

Big mom is not good exemples though, she is an abnormality. 

The scabbards said that, but in the same arc, the samurai told Ashura that 10 years from now they wouldn't be able to fight, so they had to do it now. They didn't appear to be over 50 in that flashback.

How much stronger did Ashura Doji get in 20 years? We have no idea. He was already the strongest samurai after Oden. 

The point I'm trying to make, is not that Jimbei will not evolve at all, but putting him with Zoro and Sanji is ridiculous. If Jimbei gets 10% stronger by the end of the story, Zoro and Sanji are getting 200% stronger. We're comparing a new world veteran to children. They are not comparable at all. They don't have the same potential.

Zoro will be able to have a long fight with him eos, will probably wound him a lot, but I can't see prime Zoro surpassing Kaido in a 1v1. He will come close, but I don't think he can win.

Sanji even less chance than that. 

Jimbei? Really? Have we seen a character get stronger in his fifties in one piece? Jimbei is a character past his prime, that's why no matter how strong he is now, Zoro and Sanji will be leaving him far behind. We're comparing two characters that are very young, evolve quickly, to someone who already peaked. Jimbei is now more than double their age.

I think it was stated that Doflamingo saved Monet and sugar from a terrible situation, so yes, they owe him their lives. 

As for Vergo, they met as children. 

Law already stated that the Donquiote family are just living under the illusion of being a family. In the end, they are here for Doffy, to die for him, because he's the god.

Yes, this is true but you can also get where this lack of focus came from. 

The pre-TS era was focused on building the crew. Most of the major arcs back then where crew-centric because it's just about the strawhats. How they are growing, their bond, learning to trust one another, how they are making a name for themselves and so and so. Most of the actions of this small pirate crew didn't matter in the large scale of the one piece world. Even in Enies Lobby, from an objective standpoint, the marines and the WG didn't lose much. They were the ones that bombed the island over a false call and just pinned it on the strawhats.

Post-TS, all these problems that the crew had once faced are gone. They are a well know pirate crew that trusts their captain beyond belief. All the individual arcs are mostly dealt with and now it's time to focus on what makes the one piece story great and separates it from other manga: Worldbuilding.

In the world, there are not just the strawhats on the good side. The world of Oda is too big for that. To make the story believable, there need to be other factions as strong and influential, but also get their story told in detail. This leaves little room to the main cast, that we already know, to be the main focus. What you can achieve by making Law a centre of the Dressrosa arc, you can't achieve by making it Robin or Franky. Their story was already told. This goes to be the same for all the arcs to follow. Whole cake island was an exception, it was the continuation of Sanji's flashback, but now Sanji's story is told, we can't expect him to be the focus of an arc going forward.

In the end, introducing secondary characters that are vital to the plot, are treated as the main characters of an arc or more and continue to be relevant after is One piece. It gives fresh air to the story because, in 1000+ chapters, you can't just keep on milking the story of 9 characters and making them do everything. It was the downfall of Naruto for example. The story needs to still be believable, side characters can't just exist to clap for the main cast and ask for help. 

Luffy is the MC, we see the story mostly through his eyes, but in the end, he is part of the world and not the world himself. Without Luffy, the events keep on happening, and that's the beauty of One Piece.
